examples.text: 売ってる物がバラバラなんですね。随分落ちぶれたようで。
examples.trans: You're selling quite a random assortment of things. You seem to have fallen pretty far.

examples.text: 荒波にもまれて方々にぶつかって、なめられてできたこのきれいなフォルム、非常にセクシーでございましょ？
examples.trans: Tossed by rough waves and licked smooth millions of times into this lovely form—isn't it remarkably sexy?

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
I-adjective describing beauty.

examples.trans: Mama, you're looking beautiful today too.

examples.text: 女優を美しい世界観で際立たせて見せるのが、
examples.trans: Highlighting the actress inside a gorgeous visual world

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

examples.text: 女優を美しい世界観で際立たせて見せるのが、
examples.trans: Highlighting the actress inside a gorgeous visual world

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

meanings.en: sentence-final particle of emotion or reflection
meanings.note: Colloquial particle expressing sighing, wishing, or emphasis.

examples.text: いいなあ、うらやましい。
作品の質は低いですけどね。
examples.trans: The quality of the film itself is low, though.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Connects a contrasting fact or trails off at the end of a sentence to voice a polite objection.

examples.text: お風呂に入りましたけど。
examples.trans: I already took a bath, though.

examples.text: 高いけど、おいしいです。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.

examples.text: お姉ちゃんはかわいいなあ。
examples.trans: Still, the girl herself is awfully cute.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Godan verb; past tense is 死んだ.

examples.text: 金魚が死んでしまった。

examples.trans: I don't want to die yet.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.

examples.text: これじゃダッチワイフと変わらない。
examples.trans: At this rate she's no different from a plastic doll.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
